transforms.name: plural
transforms.description: Plural form of a noun (books, boxes, cities, wolves, children, data).

transforms.name: third-person singular
transforms.description: Third-person singular present of a verb (walks, watches, tries, is, has).

transforms.name: present
transforms.description: Present tense of be other than the third-person singular (am, are).

transforms.name: past
transforms.description: Past tense of a verb, and the past participle of a regular verb (walked, stopped, tried, went, could).

transforms.name: past participle
transforms.description: Past participle of an irregular verb (taken, written, gone, been).

transforms.name: -ing
transforms.description: Present participle or gerund of a verb (walking, making, running, lying).

transforms.name: comparative
transforms.description: Comparative of an adjective or adverb (taller, nicer, happier, bigger, better).

transforms.name: superlative
transforms.description: Superlative of an adjective or adverb (tallest, nicest, happiest, biggest, best).

transforms.name: possessive
transforms.description: Possessive of a noun or name (teacher's, James', dogs').

transforms.name: contraction
transforms.description: A word with a contracted is, has, are, have, will, would, had or am ('s, 're, 've, 'll, 'd, 'm).

transforms.name: negative
transforms.description: Negative contraction of an auxiliary (don't, isn't, can't, won't).

transforms.name: interposed object
transforms.description: An object between a verb and its particle (turn it off, put Mary's coat on).

transforms.name: placeholder
transforms.description: A pronoun written as the placeholder of a dictionary entry (his temper -> one's temper, let him down -> let someone down, enjoy himself -> enjoy oneself).

transforms.name: archaic second person
transforms.description: Early Modern English second-person singular (thou walkest, thou art, thou hast).

transforms.name: archaic third person
transforms.description: Early Modern English third-person singular (he walketh, he hath, he doth).
